title: What Iraq’s US troop withdrawal means for security after Kirkuk killings
gist: As Iraq assumed full security responsibility with the US-led coalition's Sept. 30, 2026 withdrawal, a disputed Counter Terrorism Service operation in oil-rich Kirkuk — claimed to have killed Islamic State militants but alleged to have killed two Kurdish teenagers — sparked protests and raised questions about accountability, public trust and security gaps.

insights.claim: Iraq assumed full responsibility for its own security after the US-led coalition withdrew by the Sept. 30, 2026 deadline, marked by Sovereignty Day military parades.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Iraq's security forces now operate without coalition backstop, raising the importance of their competence and legitimacy for stability.

insights.claim: Some Iraqis worry that unscrupulous individuals could exploit the post-withdrawal phase as an opportunity.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: The transition window carries elevated risk of opportunistic violence or abuse of power.
insights.quote: some Iraqis worried that unscrupulous individuals could see the current phase as an opportunity to exploit

insights.claim: On Sept. 29, protests broke out in Kirkuk over the alleged killing of two Kurdish teenagers by Iraq's Counter Terrorism Service, which claimed it had killed two Islamic State affiliates and arrested a third.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: An early test of post-withdrawal security forces has produced a legitimacy crisis in a sensitive city.
insights.quote: The protests were over the alleged killing of two Kurdish teenagers by the Iraqi Counter Terrorism Service (CTS).
insights.locator: On Sept. 29, on the eve of the deadline

insights.claim: A local source said two 'terrorists wearing explosive belts' were killed but two 'children' also died in the crossfire, while others claim at least one body pictured in CTS social media photos was an innocent teenager.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Conflicting accounts and CTS's own trophy-style photos undermine public trust in Iraq's elite counterterror force.
insights.quote: two “children” had also been caught in the crossfire and lost their lives

insights.claim: Kirkuk is a key oil-rich city long disputed between Baghdad's central government and the Erbil-based Kurdistan Regional Government, making security incidents there politically charged.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Kurdish-Arab tensions in Kirkuk are a risk factor for Iraqi oil production and Baghdad-KRG relations after the coalition's exit.
insights.quote: the key oil-rich city of Kirkuk, long disputed between the central government in Baghdad and the Erbil-based Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG)
insights.locator: On Sept. 29, on the eve of the deadline
